findings.element: "+ Add condition" button / new refine row defaults
findings.finding: A newly added refine row is created already ticked ("Include refine row N") with a specific, meaningful-looking field combination pre-selected (Invoice note / contains / Memo on statement), rather than starting blank or unchecked.
findings.user_impact: A user adding a refine row to narrow the match may assume it needs configuring before it does anything, leave the defaults untouched, and unknowingly ship a live condition that changes which invoice a payment is applied to.
findings.suggested_fix: Create new refine rows unchecked (or visibly "not yet configured") until the user actively picks a source, comparison, and target, so nothing takes effect by accident.

evidence.action: Clicked "+ Add condition", then exercised refine row 1's three selects (on the payment: invoice_note → invoice_number → invoice_note; comparison: contains → eq → contains; on the invoice: private_note → doc_number → private_note).
evidence.observed: The row appeared with "Include refine row 1" already checked and all three fields holding real, specific default values (Invoice note / contains / Memo on statement) — an effective, already-active condition from the moment it's added, with no blank or clearly-inert starting state.

findings.element: "Apply as overpayment" and "Cancel sync if there is no matching open invoice found" switches (outcome cards)
findings.finding: Toggling either outcome switch produces no visible change at or near the switch itself — the description text under each switch is static regardless of state, and the only reflection of the new value is a bullet in the separate 'In plain terms' panel in the right-hand column.
findings.user_impact: Users who toggle a setting without noticing (or without a viewport wide enough to see) the sidebar summary will conclude nothing happened and may toggle it back, undoing a change that actually took effect — this is the exact 'toggle, see no effect, toggle back' pattern known to cause abandoned setup.
findings.suggested_fix: Give each switch its own inline, state-dependent confirmation right next to it (e.g. update the card's description text to name the current effect), instead of relying solely on the separate summary panel.

evidence.action: Checked "Apply as overpayment" true → false → true, and checked "Cancel sync if there is no matching open invoice found for a payment" true → false → true; both remained visible after each toggle.
evidence.observed: Neither switch's own card changed anything other than the switch's position — the description text under each ('Payment larger than the matched invoice? Post the remainder as an overpayment. Off cancels the sync instead...' / 'Same setting as Get & Send Payments...') is identical text regardless of on/off state; only the right-column 'In plain terms' list reflects the current value.

gaps: Update (save) was not exercised in this recon pass (a dedicated pass covers Close/Update). The source shows a successful save leaves the overlay open and surfaces only a small grey status line ('Applies to mzkt.by (Stripe) only.' / 'Synder's default matching stays in place.') with no explicit 'Saved' wording, toast, or persistent indicator — this lines up with the known friction of users re-opening a panel to check whether a change stuck, but I did not verify it live, so it is reported as a gap rather than a finding.

Close → 'Discard your changes?' confirmation modal was not exercised in this recon pass — its clarity, focus handling on open, and whether users understand which changes are at stake could not be verified here.

Behaviour with two or more active refine rows (the AND/OR combinator selector that only appears on the first active row once a second row is active) was not exercised in this slice — only a single refine row's controls were exercised, so consistency of that control's appearance/disappearance as rows are added or unchecked is unverified.

The 'Narrow the search' rows (Customer, Invoice date, Invoice number match checkboxes and their empty/all-off state) are not part of this slice's exercised state map, so the 'nothing set — cannot be saved' empty state and its error banner were not checked here.
